module_title: Constitutional Bodies - Judicial Interpretations and Structural Dynamics
introduction: This advanced level explores the safeguards that ensure the independence of these bodies, the evolution of their structures through Supreme Court cases, and their specific limitations in the Indian governance model.

core_concepts.title: Independence Safeguards
core_concepts.description: The expenses of UPSC and the office of CAG are 'Charged' on the Consolidated Fund of India. This means they are not voted upon by the Parliament, protecting them from financial pressure. Their service conditions cannot be varied to their disadvantage after appointment.

core_concepts.title: India vs. UK CAG
core_concepts.description: In India, the CAG is primarily an 'Auditor' who examines money AFTER it is spent. In the UK, the CAG is a true 'Controller' whose permission is required BEFORE money can be withdrawn from the treasury.

core_concepts.title: Article 149: Duties and Powers of CAG
core_concepts.description: This Article authorizes the Parliament to define the duties and powers of the CAG. This led to the enactment of the CAG (Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service) Act, 1971.

core_concepts.title: Election Commission: T.N. Seshan Legacy
core_concepts.description: Until 1989, the EC was a single-member body. It became multi-member later. The SC in the 'Dhanoa Case' and 'SS Dhanoa Case' clarified that the CEC is 'primus inter pares' (first among equals) and cannot override other commissioners.

core_concepts.title: Watchdog of the Merit System
core_concepts.description: UPSC is the 'Watchdog of the Merit System' in India. However, its role is limited regarding reservations (SC/ST/OBC) and the classification of services, which are handled by the Department of Personnel and Training (DoPT).

important_entities.name: Consolidated Fund of India
important_entities.significance: The fact that salaries of CAG and UPSC members are 'Charged' ensures that the Executive cannot use salary cuts as a threat to influence their decisions.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: The CAG's audit role is limited when it comes to 'Secret Service Expenditure'. He cannot call for particulars of expenditure but must accept a certificate from the competent administrative authority.
The Constitution mentions 'Misbehaviour or Incapacity' for SC judges and CAG, but for UPSC members, 'Misbehaviour' has a specific investigative process through the Supreme Court.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: President (Appointment), Procedure (Removal like SC judge), Purse (Charged expenditure). These three 'P's protect the EC, UPSC, and CAG.

exam_strategy_tips: In UPSC Assertion-Reasoning questions, pay attention to the fact that while the ECI implements the Model Code of Conduct, it is a consensus-based code, not a statutory law.
